target.title: fix(gateway): keep channel lifecycle outside released request admission
target.body:
Closes #110697

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where channel accounts started or restarted from a short-lived gateway request could stop accepting later work after that request finished. Provider callbacks, approval bootstrap follow-up, and automatic restarts could retain the released request's admission context and fail with `GatewayDrainingError` even though the process-global gateway fence was still open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel lifecycle work is process-lifetime, not request-lifetime. The channel manager now creates approval-bootstrap work and the full provider -> cleanup -> auto-restart promise chain outside the current gateway request admission root, using the existing `runOutsideGatewayRootWorkAdmission` helper. Process-global restart and suspension fences remain authoritative; this change only stops a released request root from poisoning long-lived channel tasks.

Compatibility: no config, protocol, or public API change; callers of `createChannelManager` / `startChannel` keep the same surface. Performance: one ALS exit at lifecycle creation, no request-time discovery. Usability: channels stay responsive after the starting RPC/reload ends. Security: does not reopen admission during real drain or suspension.

## User Impact

Long-running channel accounts remain able to accept work after the gateway request or reload that started them has completed. Real process restart and suspension still refuse new work normally.

## Evidence

Exact current head: `a73e8d29d7fbe8e245c0e37f386dc14de8f32b2d`.

- [Full CI run 29649706201](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29649706201): passed on prior head, including all four QA Smoke CI profiles.
- Focused production-patch proof on `ca8722dbbc`: `src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts` 53/53 passed; `src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts` 17/17 passed.
- Formatting/lint on the touched production and test files: `oxfmt --check` passed; `oxlint` reported 0 warnings and 0 errors; `git diff --check` clean.
- Isolated QA scenario: `qa/scenarios/channels/channel-lifecycle-admission.yaml`.

New focused cases:

1. `does not inherit a released request admission into a channel task`
2. `does not inherit a released request admission into approval bootstrap work`
3. `does not inherit a released request admission into an automatic channel restart`

## Real behavior proof

Isolated real gateway + `qa-channel` + `mock-openai` run at head `a73e8d29d7` (after the scenario harness fix that drives suspend prepare/resume over Admin HTTP, matching docs for hosts that cannot keep a WebSocket open across suspension).

Command:

```bash
OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm openclaw qa suite \
  --provider-mode mock-openai \
  --scenario channel-lifecycle-admission \
  --channel-driver qa-channel \
  --output-dir .artifacts/qa-e2e/channel-lifecycle-admission-proof3
```

Result: **passed=1 failed=0** in ~11s.

Redacted step transcript:

```text
[qa-suite] scenario pass (1/1): channel-lifecycle-admission
[qa-suite] run complete: passed=1 failed=0 skipped=0 total=1

Step 1: accepts channel work after the starting RPC root is released — pass
{
  "stopped": { "channel": "qa-channel", "accountId": "default", "stopped": true },
  "started": { "channel": "qa-channel", "accountId": "default", "started": true },
  "firstOutbound": "QA-CHANNEL-LIFECYCLE-AFTER-RPC-OK"
}

Step 2: preserves process-global suspension refusal and resumes delivery — pass
{
  "suspension": {
    "status": "ready",
    "suspensionId": "424d4adc-…-ce424fc01836",
    "activeCount": 0,
    "blockers": []
  },
  "suspendedCallError": "channels.status unavailable during gateway suspension (reason=gateway-suspending, phase=prepared)",
  "resumed": { "ok": true, "status": "running", "resumed": true },
  "resumedOutbound": "QA-CHANNEL-LIFECYCLE-AFTER-RESUME-OK"
}
```

Observable sequence matched the review acceptance criteria:

1. `channels.stop` / `channels.start` return for the real QA channel account.
2. After the start RPC root is gone, inbound work produces `QA-CHANNEL-LIFECYCLE-AFTER-RPC-OK`.
3. Prepared suspension rejects ordinary `channels.status` with `UNAVAILABLE` / `gateway-suspending`.
4. `gateway.suspend.resume` returns `running`; inbound work then produces `QA-CHANNEL-LIFECYCLE-AFTER-RESUME-OK`.

Scenario note: suite `gateway.call` opens a new WebSocket per RPC, and a prepared suspension rejects new handshakes by design (`docs/gateway/external-apps.md`). The scenario therefore enables the bundled `admin-http-rpc` plugin for prepare / refuse / resume control while still exercising the real channel delivery path on qa-channel.

## AI disclosure

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Grok and Codex).
